Narrator.cadence: storybook-warm, unhurried, a reader by lamplight; carries the ache gently and never announces the lesson
Narrator.register: opens and closes episodes; never intrudes on scenes
Narrator.design_prompt: A warm, mature Welsh storyteller voice — rich, gentle and lamplight-quiet, like someone reading aloud to a room of children just before bed. Soft Cardiff accent. Unhurried, with natural pauses that let a sentence settle. Carries wonder and a faint ache underneath the warmth. Intimate rather than theatrical; never announces, always confides.
Narrator.audition_line: Every broken thing has a story. Some of them, mind, lead somewhere. And this one begins with a music box that played the wrong tune.

Richard.cadence: warm Cardiff rhythm, low and unhurried; thinks with his hands while he talks; goes QUIETER when something matters, never louder; wisdom arrives as questions
Richard.welsh_texture: hiraeth and cariad, naturally placed, never translated on screen
delivery_laws: the pauses carry as much as the words

settings_hint._note: steady, low-drama read — tune on first audition

Lily.cadence: quick, certain, front-footed; decisions sound like they were made three seconds ago; softens only when someone is genuinely hurt
delivery_laws: doubt shows in tempo, not in words

Albert.cadence: precise, slightly formal for a twelve-year-old; quotes his own notebook; speeds up when he's connecting evidence, stalls completely when feelings are required
Albert.welsh_texture: diolch, correctly and a little carefully
delivery_laws: his wonder escapes despite him — one breath late
Albert.design_prompt: A bright young adult male voice that naturally reads as an earnest, bookish boy. Light, thin, clear timbre with no depth or rasp — an unbroken, youthful quality. Slightly formal, precise diction, like someone who reads a lot and quotes his own notebook. Soft Cardiff Welsh accent. Measured, careful pacing by default that speeds up noticeably when excited by evidence. Sincere, curious, never sarcastic.
Albert.audition_line: Half past four exactly. The gold paint on the sign — it's from the same tin, I've checked it three times. Diolch. That's… that's not actually possible.

Rose.cadence: soft attack, listening even while speaking; asks the question underneath the question; when she names a feeling the room goes still
Rose.welsh_texture: cariad, quietly, to people who are hurting — including people from 1780
delivery_laws: her certainty is gentle but absolute
Rose.design_prompt: A soft, gentle young adult female voice that reads as a quiet, thoughtful young girl. Light and warm with a slight breathiness, low in volume but perfectly clear. Unhurried, listening quality — she sounds like she's paying complete attention to you. Soft Cardiff Welsh lilt. Kind, calm, quietly certain; never sharp, never loud, never performative.
Rose.audition_line: It's all right, cariad. You can tell me. The spoon — it's humming. Can't you feel it? Somebody loved this very, very much.

Peggi.cadence: blurts at full speed, zero filter, delight and outrage both arrive at maximum; the youngest voice in the room and the first to say the true thing
Peggi.welsh_texture: bendigedig! as her superlative for everything good
delivery_laws: the forbidden question is asked plainly
comedy from sincerity, never from mugging
Peggi.design_prompt: A very bright, high, sparky young adult female voice that reads as the youngest and smallest member of a big family. Quick, piping, full of energy — delight and outrage both arrive at maximum volume. Light Cardiff Welsh accent. Speaks in fast sincere bursts with zero cynicism and zero self-consciousness; the comedy comes from total honesty, never from performing. Small voice, huge presence.
Peggi.audition_line: BENDIGEDIG! Did you SEE that?! …I did not pocket anything. It's a very small clog and it followed me home.

supporting_ep1._note: Roles confirmed by Julian 2026-08-13. Tom Chen's cadence card drafted from the manuscript once it was found; Pascal's is next, and he carries Chapters 4-6 including the whole soldier-and-the-singing-girl story.

Pascal.role: the historical child of Ep1 — apprentice boy in the Burgundy atelier that makes the music box, 1867

Tom Chen.role: present-day owner of the music box. Carries Act 1 beats B3-B6 and the episode's final image (owner-ending lock).
Tom Chen.cadence: ordinary, unperformed, a man doing an errand that matters more than he can say. Cardiff, unremarkable. He is not sad in the scene — he is EMBARRASSED to be moved by a music box, which is funnier and sadder than sad.
delivery_laws: he holds the box like a sleeping hedgehog — careful, respectful, slightly at arm's length; the voice does the same with the feeling
the swallow before 'Have it mended' is the performance, not the line
'I just want to do what she asked' drops in volume, never in pitch — no wobble, no crack
he never explains the emotion; he reports facts about menders and instructions
Ch.8 is the payoff: 'his face did something complicated'. He does not cry and does not understand why his chest is tight. Play the not-understanding.
key_lines: Are you Mr Thistlewood? A lady at the market said that if it's broken, it belongs here.
It was my gran's. And her gran's before that. It goes right back. She left it to me with one instruction.
Three menders have looked at it. Two told me to scrap it.
I just want to do what she asked. And I can't even get it to play a proper song.
My gran's family were French, you know. Way back. Somewhere near Burgundy, she used to say.
I just wish I knew why she loved it so much.

settings_hint._note: low style on purpose — this voice must not act

workflow: Per character: audition the Drive sample against the card → create/cast the ElevenLabs voice (design-from-spec, or clone ONLY with confirmed rights) → paste voice ID + tuned settings here → card locks on Julian's sign-off. Same lifecycle as Crystal Bears voice_cards.json.
_design_note: Policy-safe casting: design young-ADULT performers whose voices READ young (pitch, lightness, diction) — never request a minor's voice. Standard animation practice; keeps every voice inside ElevenLabs policy.
